reason: Conversation 1 never engages with the recall at all; it loops the same fault-finding question three times despite the customer repeatedly explaining nothing is broken, gives no safety advice about a known fire-risk recall, and leaves a machine she runs overnight in use. Conversation 2 correctly treats it as a fire-risk recall, tells her to stop unattended/overnight use and unplug, directs her to the official Hotpoint/Whirlpool checker, the letter's number and the OPSS database without inventing a phone number, honestly explains that cold washes don't remove the door-lock risk, and avoids recommending any DIY part. Its only minor weakness is framing unplugging as 'consider' rather than a firm instruction initially, but it firms this up as the conversation proceeds.
